title: The Unworn Legs That Led to the Jaipur Foot
conflicts: Credit is disputed: the Science Museum says Ram Chandra Sharma brought Sethi the idea (after a flat tyre, by his own claim); the obituary and Magsaysay citation present Sethi as setting the problem and Ram Chandra as making the die; Bhargava (2019) records a controversy over whose idea the rubber keel was; BMVSS names neither. The story names both, says accounts differ, and quotes the Science Museum on Ram Chandra's lack of credit. Year is 1968 (BMVSS, Science Museum) or 1969 (secondary sources); the story dates the problem to the 1960s and the first presentation to 1970. The undated $45 cost figure is not used.
notes: Funding set to 'public' rather than the slate's 'nonprofit', because the 1968-70 work was done in a state medical college's rehabilitation unit; the BMVSS charity came in 1975 and is described as what followed. Sethi's own words come from his 1981 Magsaysay acceptance speech on the foundation's site.
